naca0012_m015_inviscid: At $M_\infty=0.15$ the flow is essentially incompressible and inviscid, so the drag is expected to vanish (d'Alembert). The computed $C_D\approx4.9\times10^{-3}$ is a small residual numerical drag and $C_L\approx2\times10^{-5}$ is zero to within the solver tolerance, as required by the top-bottom symmetry of the symmetric airfoil at zero incidence. The residual history (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m015_inviscid_residual}) shows a monotone $\approx3.9$-order reduction to a stable plateau set by the active limiter, with stationary forces (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m015_inviscid_forces}). The Mach field is smooth and symmetric with a stagnation point at the nose (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m015_inviscid_mach_zoom}).
naca0012_m080_inviscid: At $M_\infty=0.80$ a supersonic bubble forms over the forward chord and is terminated by a symmetric normal shock near mid-chord, visible in the Mach zoom (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m080_inviscid_mach_zoom}); the flow is subsonic elsewhere and $C_L\approx2\times10^{-3}\approx0$ by symmetry. The shock produces a small wave drag, $C_D\approx8.7\times10^{-3}$. This case converged rapidly (2826 steps, $\approx3.9$ orders) because the inviscid transonic residual is well conditioned.
naca0012_m200_inviscid: At $M_\infty=2.0$ a detached bow shock stands ahead of the leading edge with a subsonic pocket behind it and oblique shocks/expansion along the chord (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m200_inviscid_mach_zoom}). The wave drag $C_D\approx9.1\times10^{-2}$ dominates and $C_L\approx4\times10^{-4}\approx0$. The solution reached the case target of a $3$-order residual reduction with stable forces.
naca0012_m015_laminar_re5000: The subsonic laminar case at $Re=5000$ develops a thin attached boundary layer near the leading edge that separates laminarly over the forward mid-chord and remains separated to the trailing edge (near-zero skin friction over the aft chord in \texttt{surface.csv}), with a symmetric wake (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m015_laminar_re5000_mach_zoom}). The drag $C_D\approx7.8\times10^{-3}$ and $C_L\approx-3\times10^{-4}\approx0$; the no-slip wall rows report exactly zero wall velocity with nonzero skin friction (see sanity checks). Because the separated state equilibrates slowly, the settled value was verified by restarting the converged state for a further $8000$ pseudo-steps: $C_D$ stayed in the band $0.0076$--$0.0079$, bracketing the reported value (see \S\ref{sec:limitations}).
naca0012_m080_laminar_re5000: This transonic laminar case combines a shock-induced pressure rise with a low-Reynolds-number boundary layer; the result is massive shock-induced separation over the aft chord (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m080_laminar_re5000_mach_zoom}). The smooth Venkatakrishnan limiter is used because the non-smooth Barth--Jespersen limiter produced a limit cycle that stalled the residual near $2.8$ orders. The separated state equilibrates very slowly: the production run therefore uses a longer horizon ($25000$ steps; see run manifest) and terminates on a force plateau, $C_D=0.0399\pm0.5\%$ over the final $5000$ steps, with a bounded residual reduction of $3.2$ orders (the separated bubble sustains a small persistent residual, so the case's $4$-order target is not reachable once the separation forms; the force plateau is the physical convergence criterion here, \S\ref{sec:limitations}). The settled state is mildly symmetry-broken, $C_L\approx+2.6\times10^{-2}$ at zero incidence -- a known feature of low-Reynolds-number separated airfoil flow. Relative to an earlier production attempt stopped at the case target ($C_D=0.064$), the fully settled drag is $\approx38\%$ lower, which is why the deep-convergence settings are used for this case.
naca0012_m200_laminar_re5000: The supersonic laminar case shows a detached bow shock and a thick low-Mach viscous shroud that engulfs the airfoil: the boundary layer separates at the nose and the whole body sits inside a slow recirculating layer, so the skin friction is near zero over most of the chord and the drag is pressure-dominated (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m200_laminar_re5000_mach_zoom}). This is the stiffest case in the set: with Roe flux and Barth--Jespersen limiter the pseudo-time iteration diverges late (after the plateau is reached) unless the pseudo-CFL is kept below $\approx10$, so production uses the documented stiff-case recipe (Rusanov flux, Venkatakrishnan limiter, CFL cap $10$), which converges cleanly by $5.6$ orders over $20000$ steps to $C_D=0.102\pm0.2\%$ with $C_L\approx+7\times10^{-4}\approx0$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:naca0012_m200_laminar_re5000_forces}). A Roe-flux restart chain to the same plateau gives $C_D\approx0.088$, i.e.\ the settled drag of this massively separated state carries a $\sim15\%$ flux-model uncertainty (\S\ref{sec:limitations}).
cylinder_m010_laminar_re20: The cylinder at $Re=20$ converges to a steady, symmetric wake: $C_L\approx5\times10^{-3}\approx0$ and the lift/drag histories are stationary (Fig.~\ref{fig:cylinder_m010_laminar_re20_forces}). A closed recirculation bubble forms behind the cylinder (Fig.~\ref{fig:cylinder_m010_laminar_re20_mach_zoom}); the wall pressure coefficient peaks at the front stagnation point ($C_p\approx1$) and is symmetric top-bottom. This stiff low-Mach viscous case required the Rusanov flux, the smooth Venkatakrishnan limiter, and a conservative pseudo-CFL cap to avoid a spurious limit cycle (see \S\ref{sec:limitations}); it then converged by $5.0$ orders. The drag $C_D\approx0.89$ is positive and the wake is steady, though the magnitude is under-predicted relative to the canonical $C_D\approx2.0$ because of low-Mach numerical dissipation (\S\ref{sec:limitations}).
cylinder_m010_laminar_re200: The cylinder at $Re=200$ is run as a true BDF2 dual-time transient ($\Delta t=0.01$, $t_f=300$, $30{,}000$ physical steps, inner LU-SGS solve to a $10^{-3}$ total-residual reduction per step). After the initial transient a self-sustained von K\'arm\'an vortex street develops: the lift oscillates periodically (Fig.~\ref{fig:cylinder_m010_laminar_re200_forces}) and the post-transient vorticity field (Fig.~\ref{fig:cylinder_m010_laminar_re200_vorticity_wake}) shows the alternating signed vortices convecting downstream. The measured Strouhal number, mean drag, and lift amplitude are reported in the summary line above and in Table~\ref{tab:results}; the shedding frequency is extracted from the post-transient lift history by an FFT. The drag magnitude is under-predicted relative to incompressible references ($C_D\approx1.3$) owing to low-Mach dissipation (\S\ref{sec:limitations}), but the shedding frequency and flow structure are correct.
